name: Computer Science
boundaries: Computer Science: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Resolution of P versus NP, either direction
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part by CSC-01. The constructive, feasible-algorithm half is CSC-01. The P ≠ NP half is not added. Cook places the practical upset at a constructive proof of P = NP, and a separation alone would confirm a limit that practice already assumes. It would not secure cryptography. The 2024 Journal of Cryptology abstract still treats one-way functions from average-case hardness as open, which is the Pessiland gap.

original_dispositions.original_title: Explicit construction of one-way functions from minimal assumptions, proved without conjectures such as factoring
original_dispositions.reason: The underlying concept was already rejected in the first pass and stays rejected. An unconditional proof would be a foundational theorem. Deployed systems already use candidate one-way functions. Public-key encryption is a further assumption beyond one-way functions, so the historical impact sentence overshoots the theorem. The result is also incompatible with CSC-01. No separate ID.

original_dispositions.original_title: Practical fully homomorphic encryption with polylog overhead
original_dispositions.reason: The concept is routine-cost general computation on encrypted data. The specific polylogarithm was not verified in a primary source and is not the completion criterion. Existence of FHE is already achieved and is not a separate entry.

Gidney’s 2025 estimate is under one million noisy qubits for 2048-bit factoring under explicit assumptions, and no inspected source shows an exponential quantum algorithm for NP-complete problems. Drug design, materials, and logistics need further breakthroughs beyond the computer. Those corrections are written into CSC-02. The entry is not replaced.

Matrix multiplication is in P. The best bound whose abstract was read in this revision is ω < 2.371177, improving 2.371339. An unopened October 2026 preprint is not used as a bound. Even a proved exponent of 2 would be a polynomial improvement inside P. The laser-method algorithms that produce these exponents are not the algorithms numerical software runs. This reorganizes algebraic complexity but does not create a new general capability at the calibration bar.

original_dispositions.original_title: Resolution of the Unique Games Conjecture
original_dispositions.reason: A proof would tighten approximability for many optimization problems. The PCP theorem already supplied the general reduction framework, and the 2-to-2 games theorem is already proved. The missing step is a classification result, not a new computing capability, and it would not prove P ≠ NP. An October 2026 announcement of a proof was not independently reviewed here, and the Lean development was not checked.

original_dispositions.original_title: Formalization and proof or disproof of the physical extended Church–Turing thesis
original_dispositions.reason: The complexity-theoretic formulation already exists. Bernstein and Vazirani gave oracle evidence against efficient classical simulation and showed why an unrelativized proof needs a further complexity breakthrough, because BQP sits inside P^#P. A physical demonstration that a useful quantum computation is not efficiently classically simulable is the content of CSC-02. A device that computes beyond the quantum model would be physics. Neither remainder is a separate computer-science capability.

original_dispositions.original_title: Efficient Byzantine fault tolerance at internet scale with constant or polylogarithmic communication, one-third malicious parties, and millions of nodes
original_dispositions.reason: Deterministic authenticated Byzantine agreement already has a quadratic message lower bound when the number of faults grows linearly with the number of parties. The historical communication target conflicts with that bound. Internet-scale consensus protocols already exist. What remains is performance, incentives, and proof of particular systems. Randomized models can change the expected-message bound; this revision did not re-derive those newer bounds and does not claim they restore constant or polylogarithmic communication at a one-third fault rate.

original_dispositions.original_title: Strong unconditional circuit lower bounds such as P not contained in NC¹, or P ≠ P/poly, avoiding known barriers
original_dispositions.reason: Williams showed that NEXP does not have nonuniform polynomial-size ACC circuits. NP versus polynomial-size circuits remains open, and a proof would imply P ≠ NP, so it sits with the rejected P ≠ NP entry rather than with a new capability. A separation explains a limit. It does not by itself redesign hardware or prove a limitation of neural networks.

original_dispositions.original_title: A general efficient framework that automatically generates fine-grained conditional lower bounds
original_dispositions.reason: The framework already exists. Vassilevska Williams’s ICM 2018 survey describes fine-grained reductions and tight conditional lower bounds. The hypotheses remain open. An automatic generator of further reductions would be a tool inside that theory. The full ICM paper body was not line-read.

reconciliation_change_log.change: 2026-11-01. Initial note. Ten candidates selected after source checks of P versus NP, fault-tolerant quantum hardware, general-intelligence evaluations, seL4 and CompCert, homomorphic encryption, generalization surveys, formal mathematics through the September 2026 Fermat and Navier–Stokes announcements, robot generalization benchmarks, indistinguishability obfuscation, and neural-network verification scale.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The bar is a change inside computer science comparable to a new principle, a new general capability, or a collapse in cost that turns a known idea into infrastructure.

reconciliation_change_log.change: 2026-11-01, revision. All ten IDs kept. No concept deleted, replaced, or merged. No CSC-11 or later ID added.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The ten first-pass concepts are unchanged in identity. Historical items 1, 3, and 4 sit inside CSC-01, CSC-05, and CSC-02, with the overclaims corrected. The other historical items are real open problems or already-built theory, and they stay below the capability bar used here.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CSC-01 clarified. The entry remains a feasible constructive algorithm. A bare proof of P ≠ NP is explicitly outside it.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Impagliazzo’s Pessiland, as described in the 2024 Journal of Cryptology abstract and in 2026 course notes of the 1995 paper, blocks the claim that P ≠ NP would secure cryptography. Clay’s page was re-opened and is still marked Unsolved.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CSC-02 clarified. Gidney’s figure is less than one million noisy qubits under stated assumptions, not millions of logical qubits. Drug, materials, and logistics outcomes are marked as requiring further work. Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard, and Vazirani’s random-oracle bound is added. A demonstrated break of efficient classical simulation is treated as this entry’s content, not as a new ID.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The entry should not inherit a claim of exponential speedup for NP-complete problems.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CSC-05 clarified. The completion criterion remains the proposed factor of ten.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical “polylog overhead” number was not found in a primary source and is not adopted.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CSC-07 updated. Clay’s 11 September 2026 Navier–Stokes notice was opened. The OpenAI claim stays a company claim.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The notice says the problem has apparently been settled and that the prize process is unhurried. It does not award a prize. MathWorld, read the same day, still shows the problem as Active.

reconciliation_change_log.change: CSC-10 corrected. Huang, Ruan, Huang, Jin, Dong, Wu, Bensalem, Mu, Qi, Zhao, and further coauthors are now named from the Liverpool repository, with DOI 10.1007/s10462-024-10824-0. reconciliation_change_log.reason: The white-box sentence was not re-found in an open full text.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Historical source check. The five supporting URLs in the historical list do not establish that list.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The live document closest to a 2026 grand-challenge statement is Regli and coauthors, which asks the community to define such challenges and does not list those ten items.
